_comment: UK DESNZ/Defra GHG conversion factors 2025 — modal_default freight rows.
Primary source: 'Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2025' (DESNZ), published 2025-06-10.
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/greenhouse-gas-reporting-conversion-factors-2025
'full set (for advanced users)' xlsx:
https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6846a4f55e92539572806125/ghg-conversion-factors-2025-full-set.xlsx
PROVENANCE: [CONFIRMED] against the primary workbook on 2026-08-30.
The workbook (1,796,009 bytes) was fetched in-browser from assets.publishing.service.gov.uk,
unzipped by a manual ZIP central-directory walk + DecompressionStream('deflate-raw'), and the
sheet resolved BY NAME through xl/workbook.xml + xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels:
'Freighting goods' -> rId31 -> xl/worksheets/sheet31.xml   (never resolved by position)
Header block: row 25 (Activity | Type | Unit | kg CO2e ...). Factor set 'Full set', Year 2025,
Version 1, next publication June 2026 (row 5-6 of the same sheet).
THE COLUMN TRAP THIS VERIFICATION CAUGHT, recorded so nobody re-reads the wrong cell:
The 'Freighting goods' sheet does NOT use one column layout throughout. Row 24 blocks the VANS
section by FUEL (D=Diesel, H=Petrol, L=CNG, P=LPG, T=Unknown, X=PHEV, AB=BEV). Rows 40 and 68
re-block the HGV sections by LADEN PERCENTAGE (D=0% Laden, H=50% Laden, L=100% Laden,
P=Average laden), each followed by its own repeated header row (41, 69).
So for every HGV row below, the average-laden total kg CO2e is column P, NOT column D.
Column D on an HGV tonne.km row is 0% Laden and is EMPTY by construction (zero tonnes carried).
Rail (row 105-106) uses the plain D/E/F/G layout again.
WHAT THE VERIFICATION FOUND: all four previous values were WRONG. They came from a third-party
republication (github.com/starrybodies/ghg-calculator, defra/v2025.json) that cites DEFRA 2025
but does not reproduce it. Measured against the primary, per row:
Rigid (>7.5t-17t)   fixture 0.296  vs primary 0.36362  -> fixture was 18.6% LOW
Articulated (>33t)  fixture 0.091  vs primary 0.07703  -> fixture was 18.1% HIGH
All HGVs            fixture 0.115  vs primary 0.10163  -> fixture was 13.2% HIGH
Rail freight train  fixture 0.024  vs primary 0.02779  -> fixture was 13.6% LOW
No laden column (0%/50%/100%/Average) reproduces the old numbers either, so they are not a
mis-picked column of the 2025 set; they appear to be a different year or derivation entirely.
The gate in this file's previous header ('verify each ttw_co2e before --apply') is the reason
four incorrect origin_class='official' factors did not reach production. It did its job.
INTERNAL CONSISTENCY CHECK performed on the primary, independent of the totals above: for each
row the three per-gas columns sum to the published total, which confirms the correct cells were
read rather than a plausible-looking neighbour:
gwp_basis: 'AR5_GWP100', no longer 'unstated'. The workbook states it verbatim (sharedStrings
index 620): 'The GWPs used in the calculation of CO2e are based on the Intergovernmental Panel
on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report (AR5) over a 100-year period'.
PER-GAS COLUMNS ARE POPULATED, and the semantic question that previously blocked them is RESOLVED.
The question was whether co2_fossil/ch4/n2o mean raw gas MASS or an already-GWP-weighted CO2e
value, since no column comment says. The EPA fixture answers it definitively and arithmetically:
its own header states ttw_co2e = co2_fossil + ch4_kg*28 + n2o_kg*265, and its live rows satisfy
that identity exactly (0.1274 + 1.1e-6*28 + 3.7e-6*265 = 0.128411, the published total). So the
columns are GAS MASS and ttw_co2e is the GWP-weighted sum. Guessing would have been a ~28x silent
unit error on CH4; the answer was recoverable from a sibling fixture instead.
DESNZ publishes its per-gas columns the OTHER way, as 'kg CO2e of CH4 per unit' (already
GWP-weighted), so each is divided by its AR5 GWP-100 coefficient to recover mass:
ch4_mass = (kg CO2e of CH4) / 28      n2o_mass = (kg CO2e of N2O) / 265
co2_fossil is taken as published: CO2 has GWP 1, so its CO2e column IS its mass.
This is an exact unit conversion with a stated divisor, not a model — anyone can invert it. The
divisors are the same AR5 GWP-100 values the workbook itself declares (see gwp_basis below), so
the conversion uses the source's own basis rather than one we chose.
ROUNDED TO 3 SIGNIFICANT FIGURES, because DESNZ publishes the CH4 column to as little as ONE
significant figure (8e-5 kg CO2e/tonne.km) and carrying more digits would invent precision the
source does not have. Reconciliation after rounding, worst case +1.31e-5 on the rigid row:
NOTE the articulated row does not reconcile exactly even BEFORE rounding (0.07702 vs a published
0.07703). That gap is DESNZ's own rounding in its per-gas columns, not ours. ttw_co2e is kept as
PUBLISHED in every row — the per-gas columns are never allowed to restate the headline figure.
as_at_date / valid_from: 2025-06-10, the DESNZ publication date for the 2025 factor set.
derivation: 'observed' — the ttw_co2e value is used as published by the primary source, not
recomputed by us (contrast the EPA fixture, which IS a derived/calculated conversion).
=== 2026-09-02, lane PROD-FIX: AIR AND SEA ROWS — NEEDS RUNNER FETCH, no figures added ===
The 'Freighting goods' sheet also carries Air and Sea/Ocean sections; this fixture had none. The
brief asked for: air (domestic, short-haul international, long-haul international, per tonne.km,
split 'with RF'/'without RF' if the sheet distinguishes them) and sea (container ship average,
bulk carrier average, general cargo average, RoRo, per tonne.km).
EVERY reachable route to the primary was tried this session and every one failed at the same edge —
this container's egress, not the publisher:
1. WebFetch on the gov.uk publication page: SUCCEEDED, and returned the same full-set xlsx URL
already cited above (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6846a4f55e92539572806125/
ghg-conversion-factors-2025-full-set.xlsx) plus a condensed-set and a 'flat format' xlsx — no
CSV of this dataset is published anywhere (checked the publication page, the collection page,
and a web search for a data.gov.uk mirror; none exists).
2. WebFetch directly on that xlsx URL: returns the literal string '[binary data]', twice, with two
different prompts. WebFetch extracts text from HTML and from PDF (confirmed: the methodology
PDF fetched as readable text) but has no xlsx text extraction, so the cell data is unreachable
through it.
3. Direct curl from this container to assets.publishing.service.gov.uk: 'CONNECT tunnel failed,
response 403' — the org egress proxy does not allowlist that host (confirmed via
$HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status: only npm/pypi/crates/anthropic-API hosts are listed).
4. The same curl re-tried from the session's connected device (a second machine, its own egress):
identical 'Received HTTP code 403 from proxy after CONNECT' — the device shell sits behind the
same org/account allowlist, not a separate one, per its own tool description.
So this is the fixture-header fallback the brief names, not a shortcut: the seven rows below are
SHELLS ONLY. Every field a runner would need to confirm from the primary (the figure itself, the
gas split, energy_carrier, gwp_basis, pedigree, derivation, origin_class, method_version) is null.
Only the fields this session can stand behind without reading the workbook are filled: tier/
scope_kind/mode (the shape the brief specifies), vehicle_class (the category label the brief names,
not a measured figure), jurisdiction ('GB', same as every other row in this GB-only fixture),
quantity_basis ('tonne_km', per the brief), and as_at_date/valid_from (2025-06-10, the publication
date already confirmed for this fixture's header, not row-specific). NOTHING numeric is invented.
Each pending row carries needs_runner_fetch: true and a source_ref beginning 'NEEDS RUNNER FETCH:'.
emission-factors-desnz.test.mjs enforces that a row may have ttw_co2e null ONLY when
needs_runner_fetch is true, and that every OTHER row's source_ref cites a sheet name and a row
number, so a future row added without either guard fails the test rather than silently seeding.
emission-factors-desnz.mjs filters needs_runner_fetch rows out of the seed batch and logs them,
so a producer run still seeds the 4 confirmed rows and never attempts to write a shell.
OPEN QUESTION for the runner, not answered here: whether the Air section splits into 'with RF' and
'without RF' variants (as DESNZ's Business travel — air tables do) or reports one figure per haul
length. The three air shells below are the minimum the brief asks for; if the sheet does carry an
RF split, the runner should replace each with a _with_rf/_without_rf pair (six rows, not three) —
do not guess which shape is correct without opening the sheet.
